REASONING:
**Step 1 – Frame the project**  
- **Objective:** Improve quality of school education and expand access to science & commerce senior‑secondary education in Chhattisgarh.  
- **Scope & Components:** Four Results Areas – (RA‑1) teacher professional development & TaRL; (RA‑2) student diagnostic & remedial assessment system; (RA‑3) model composite school development (disaster‑resilient, energy‑efficient); (RA‑4) school leadership (DRM, SRGBV). Includes IPF‑TA technical assistance, EMIS development, procurement of civil works, training modules, and monitoring.  
- **Delivery model:** State Implementation Society for Samagra Shiksha (SIS‑SS) as nodal implementer; sub‑implementers SCERT, SIEMAT, DIETs, PWD, RES; Project Management Consultant (PMC) and Independent Verification Agency (IVA) engaged.  
- **Timeline:** July 2023 – December 2028 (5 years).  
- **Budget:** Total operation US$558.3 M; CHALK program US$535.8 M; IBRD loan US$300 M; counterpart funding US$258.3 M.  
- **Key stakeholders:** GoCG (DoSE, DoSE&L), SCERT, SIEMAT, DIETs, PWD, RES, World Bank, PMC, IVA, teachers, school management committees, students, community groups.  
- **External dependencies:** State budget cycles, Samagra Shiksha (SS) financing, e‑Government Procurement (e‑GP) & GeM portals, climate‑related disruptions, data‑protection legislation.

**Step 2 – Category sweep (candidate risks with supporting text)**  
- *Technical*: EMIS capacity gap (Sec 41); lack of standardized assessment data (Sec 13); no structured TaRL training program (DLI 4 baseline); absence of annual procurement plan (Sec 4.5).  
- *Financial*: Fiduciary risk rated “Substantial” (Sec 56); budgeting and fund‑release delays due to multi‑tier planning (Sec 59).  
- *Schedule*: Climate‑induced drought/flood risk affecting construction and school days (Sec 3); DLI verification may delay disbursements (DLIs verification protocol).  
- *Stakeholder*: Teacher shortage/high pupil‑teacher ratios (Sec 11); community preference for boys to work, no residential schools for boys (Sec 6); weak grievance redress mechanism (Sec 67).  
- *Political/Regulatory*: Potential new personal‑data protection law impacting data handling (Legal covenants Sec III.C).  
- *Environmental*: Construction waste, pollution, fire‑safety gaps (Sec 70); broader climate change impacts (Sec 72).  
- *Organizational*: SIS‑SS staffed at ~70 % of sanctioned strength (Sec 14); internal‑audit/control weaknesses (Sec 15).  
- *External*: Under‑funded technical support agencies limiting capacity (Sec 4.4).

**Step 3 – Evidence filter**  
All listed risks are directly quoted in the appraisal document; none are removed.

**Step 4 – Assess & mitigate**  

| ID | Likelihood (1‑5) | Impact (1‑5) | Justification (likelihood / impact) | Mitigation (concrete) |
|----|------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| R01 | 4 | 4 | Capacity gaps are explicit and central to EMIS rollout. | Assign dedicated EMIS team, embed technical experts via IPF‑TA, set phased milestones, monitor through PMC. |
| R02 | 3 | 4 | Current assessment system is weak; improvement planned but not yet in place. | Strengthen SCERT Assessment Cell, launch periodic SLAS, train staff on item‑level data, integrate with EMIS. |
| R03 | 4 | 3 | No existing TaRL programme; development required. | Fast‑track curriculum design, allocate blended‑learning resources, monitor trainer deployment, set completion checkpoints. |
| R04 | 3 | 3 | Procurement plan absent; could cause delays. | Draft and approve annual procurement plan per FMP manual, assign procurement specialist, track against timeline. |
| R05 | 3 | 4 | “Substantial” fiduciary risk identified. | Implement IFSA recommendations, augment FM staff, conduct regular internal audits, enforce strict controls. |
| R06 | 4 | 3 | Multi‑tier budgeting repeatedly causes release delays. | Streamline AWP&B approval (target ≤ 3 months), provide budgeting capacity‑building, use interim financing where needed. |
| R07 | 3 | 4 | State prone to droughts/floods; construction sensitive to weather. | Use disaster‑resilient designs, schedule works in optimal seasons, maintain buffer time in Gantt. |
| R08 | 3 | 3 | DLI verification requires field surveys that may lag. | Strengthen verification team, use digital data submission, schedule verification early in fiscal year. |
| R09 | 4 | 4 | Teacher shortage documented; high pupil‑teacher ratios. | Accelerate recruitment, offer contract teachers, provide incentives for subject specialists, use remote training modules. |
| R10 | 3 | 3 | Social norm pushes boys to work; no residential schools for boys. | Community‑engagement campaigns, develop boys’ residential facilities, provide scholarships/incentives. |
| R11 | 3 | 2 | GRM currently weak; could affect community trust. | Upgrade GRM to online portal, set response‑time SLA, train staff, publish regular reports. |
| R12 | 2 | 3 | New data‑protection law uncertain but possible. | Conduct legal impact analysis, update data‑handling SOPs, train staff on compliance, embed safeguards in contracts. |
| R13 | 3 | 3 | Construction may generate waste, fire‑safety gaps. | Adopt environmental management plan, enforce waste segregation, include fire‑safety standards in designs, train contractors. |
| R14 | 4 | 4 | Climate change projected to increase extreme events. | Climate‑risk screening for sites, incorporate green building features, develop school emergency response plans. |
| R15 | 3 | 3 | SIS‑SS operating at 70 % staffing. | Recruit to fill vacancies, offer retention incentives, cross‑train existing staff. |
| R16 | 3 | 3 | Internal‑audit controls not fully applied. | Establish dedicated internal‑audit unit, adopt risk‑based audit schedule, ensure audit‑observation follow‑up. |
| R17 | 3 | 3 | Technical agencies under‑funded, limiting scalability. | Secure multi‑year funding agreements, build in‑house capacity, monitor deliverables against milestones. |

**Step 5 – Consolidate**  
All 17 risks are retained; no duplicates identified.
